voor.The expedition was not only a race: You'd find microscopes and notebooks packed beside the sledges.
voor.The youngest officer later wrote: You might have read it yourself, or heard of its famous title.
voor.In a great storm, the men saved: You'd feel the cold water sloshing around your ankles as you passed the bucket along.
voor.Scott chose a cape of black sand: You'd see the dark beach stand out sharply against all that white.
voor.The scientists fished through holes: You'd sit beside a hole in the ice, waiting for a tug on your line.
voor.Killer whales once tried: You'd hear a great thump under the ice beneath your feet.
voor.The untidiest corner of the hut: You'd see boots, books and socks tumbling out of every bunk.
voor.Little pens in the scientists' corner: You'd hear them scratching softly through the night.
voor.One pony was so wild: You'd laugh to see four grown men hanging on to one small pony.
voor.Snow petrels flew over the ice: You'd see them flicker past, pale against the blue sky.
voor.Wilson believed the largest penguin: You can picture him, eyes shining, explaining his idea.
voor.In a blizzard, the men tied themselves: You'd hold the rope tight and follow it, step by step.
voor.Through all that cold and darkness: You might expect them to argue. They never did.
voor.The road to the Pole had three parts: You'd see the route drawn out on a map pinned to the wall.
voor.A short telegram had told Scott: You can imagine him reading it twice, very quietly.
voor.The motor sledges set out first: You'd hear them clattering and coughing across the ice.
voor.At the Pole, Amundsen left a small tent: You'd find it flapping in the wind, all alone.
voor.Scott's party left with the ponies: You'd see the line stretch out across the white plain.
voor.A four-day blizzard trapped them: You'd lie in your sleeping bag, listening to the wind roar.
voor.When the last support team turned home: You'd see them shake hands, one by one, in the cold.
voor.Bowers walked the plateau on foot: You'd hear his steady footsteps beside the skis.
voor.On the plateau, the wind carved: You'd stumble over the hard ridges again and again.
voor.Fifteen miles from the Pole: You'd see a tiny dark speck against all that white.
voor.On the way home, they rigged a sail: You'd feel the sledge glide a little more easily.
voor.Cherry waited six days: You'd see him lift the telescope again and again, hoping.
voor.The search party built a tall cairn: You'd see it standing alone on the wide white plain.
voor.On a hill above the ice, the men carved: If you climbed that hill, you'd find the cross still standing.
voor.The fossil leaves they carried: You might think a few stones couldn't matter much. They mattered a great deal.
